pr.title: Fix Date.to_iso8601/2 loses :format with custom calendar
pr.description: Date.to_iso8601/2 loses the requested :format for a date built with a non-ISO calendar. Calling to_iso8601(date, :basic) on such a date silently returned the :extended representation instead of the requested :basic one. The change preserves the requested format when converting the date to the ISO calendar first, and adds a regression test.
pr.diff:
diff --git a/lib/elixir/lib/calendar/date.ex b/lib/elixir/lib/calendar/date.ex
index ad709413306..cbdbcf07bee 100644
--- a/lib/elixir/lib/calendar/date.ex
+++ b/lib/elixir/lib/calendar/date.ex
@@ -422,7 +422,7 @@ defmodule Date do
   def to_iso8601(%{calendar: _} = date, format) when format in [:basic, :extended] do
     date
     |> convert!(Calendar.ISO)
-    |> to_iso8601()
+    |> to_iso8601(format)
   end
 
   @doc """
diff --git a/lib/elixir/test/elixir/calendar/date_test.exs b/lib/elixir/test/elixir/calendar/date_test.exs
index c7d33533335..81a233133f5 100644
--- a/lib/elixir/test/elixir/calendar/date_test.exs
+++ b/lib/elixir/test/elixir/calendar/date_test.exs
@@ -38,6 +38,16 @@ defmodule DateTest do
     end
   end
 
+  test "to_iso8601/2" do
+    date = ~D[2000-01-01]
+    assert Date.to_iso8601(date) == "2000-01-01"
+    assert Date.to_iso8601(date, :basic) == "20000101"
+
+    holo_date = Calendar.Holocene.date(12001, 1, 1)
+    assert Date.to_iso8601(holo_date) == "2001-01-01"
+    assert Date.to_iso8601(holo_date, :basic) == "20010101"
+  end
+
   test "to_string/1" do
     date = ~D[2000-01-01]
     assert to_string(date) == "2000-01-01"

testCase.title: Formatting a non-Gregorian-calendar date in basic ISO 8601 style
testCase.preconditions: A Date value has been built using an alternate (non-default, non-ISO) calendar implementation, representing the same day as January 1st of the year 2001 in the standard calendar.
steps: Convert the date to its ISO 8601 string representation with no format argument (the default, extended, form).
Note the returned string.
Convert the same date to its ISO 8601 string representation again, this time explicitly requesting the basic (no separators) format.
Compare the two returned strings.
testCase.expectedResult: The default call returns "2001-01-01" (extended form, with dashes). The explicit basic-format call returns "20010101" (compact form, no dashes) — the requested basic format is honored rather than the result silently falling back to the extended form.

metadata.feature: Date ISO8601 formatting with custom calendars

provenance.note: The PR adds a test asserting Date.to_iso8601/2 preserves the requested :basic/:extended format for a date built with a non-ISO calendar; at the base commit the basic-format call incorrectly returns the extended-format string, so the assertion (and this equivalent behavior check) fails.

pr.title: #3307 Fix ->end property not updating after setEndDate() on PHP 8.2+
pr.description: On PHP 8.2+, a date-period object's native `end` property is managed internally by the engine and cannot be written directly after construction. Calling the method that updates the period's end date correctly updated the object's internal end-date state but left the native `end` property showing the original value from construction. The fix re-synchronizes the native property after start/end date updates, and adds a regression test.

testCase.title: Reading a date range's end value after changing its end date
testCase.preconditions: A date-range/period object has been created spanning 2024-09-01 to 2024-09-30, running on PHP 8.2 or later.
steps: Call the method that updates the period's end date, setting it to 2025-06-15.
Read the period's end date via its `end` property.
Read the period's end date via its `getEndDate()` accessor method.
testCase.expectedResult: Both the `end` property and the `getEndDate()` accessor report the newly set end date, 2025-06-15 00:00:00 — not the original end date (2024-09-30) that was set when the period was first constructed.

provenance.note: The PR adds testEndPropertySyncsAfterSetEndDate, asserting `->end` reflects the date passed to the end-date setter. At the base commit, on PHP 8.2+, the `end` property still reports the original construction-time value while `getEndDate()` reports the update, so the two disagree and the check fails.

pr.title: Prevent CRLF injection due to broken URL normalizer
pr.description: If a custom URL normalizer does not filter out whitespace, the client would previously happily transmit a request line containing embedded whitespace, including newline characters. Whitespace, in particular a literal newline, is never allowed in a request's path, query, or hostname. The change raises an error before the request is sent if the resolved path or host contains whitespace, and adds regression specs. Not a security fix in itself but an extra line of defence.
pr.diff:
diff --git a/lib/http/request.rb b/lib/http/request.rb
index 1372cd11..39dd6b1c 100644
--- a/lib/http/request.rb
+++ b/lib/http/request.rb
@@ -172,7 +172,9 @@ def headline
           uri.omit(:fragment)
         else
           uri.request_uri
-        end
+        end.to_s
+
+      raise RequestError, "Invalid request URI: #{request_uri.inspect}" if request_uri.match?(/\s/)
 
       "#{verb.to_s.upcase} #{request_uri} HTTP/#{version}"
     end
@@ -230,7 +232,11 @@ def port
 
     # @return [String] Default host (with port if needed) header value.
     def default_host_header_value
-      PORTS[@scheme] == port ? host : "#{host}:#{port}"
+      value = PORTS[@scheme] == port ? host : "#{host}:#{port}"
+
+      raise RequestError, "Invalid host: #{value.inspect}" if value.match?(/\s/)
+
+      value
     end
 
     def prepare_body(body)
diff --git a/spec/lib/http_spec.rb b/spec/lib/http_spec.rb
index f7a1bb21..746a08ec 100644
--- a/spec/lib/http_spec.rb
+++ b/spec/lib/http_spec.rb
@@ -460,20 +460,37 @@ def setsockopt(*args)
 
     context "with :normalize_uri" do
       it "normalizes URI" do
-        response = HTTP.get "#{dummy.endpoint}/hello world"
+        response = HTTP.get "#{dummy.endpoint}/héllö-wörld"
         expect(response.to_s).to eq("hello world")
       end
 
       it "uses the custom URI Normalizer method" do
         client = HTTP.use(:normalize_uri => {:normalizer => :itself.to_proc})
-        response = client.get("#{dummy.endpoint}/hello world")
+        response = client.get("#{dummy.endpoint}/héllö-wörld")
         expect(response.status).to eq(400)
       end
 
+      it "raises if custom URI Normalizer returns invalid path" do
+        client = HTTP.use(:normalize_uri => {:normalizer => :itself.to_proc})
+        expect { client.get("#{dummy.endpoint}/hello\nworld") }.
+          to raise_error HTTP::RequestError, 'Invalid request URI: "/hello\nworld"'
+      end
+
+      it "raises if custom URI Normalizer returns invalid host" do
+        normalizer = lambda do |uri|
+          uri.port = nil
+          uri.instance_variable_set(:@host, "example\ncom")
+          uri
+        end
+        client = HTTP.use(:normalize_uri => {:normalizer => normalizer})
+        expect { client.get(dummy.endpoint) }.
+          to raise_error HTTP::RequestError, 'Invalid host: "example\ncom"'
+      end
+
       it "uses the default URI normalizer" do
         client = HTTP.use :normalize_uri
         expect(HTTP::URI::NORMALIZER).to receive(:call).and_call_original
-        response = client.get("#{dummy.endpoint}/hello world")
+        response = client.get("#{dummy.endpoint}/héllö-wörld")
         expect(response.to_s).to eq("hello world")
       end
     end
diff --git a/spec/support/dummy_server/servlet.rb b/spec/support/dummy_server/servlet.rb
index 9f835c33..81e32ab4 100644
--- a/spec/support/dummy_server/servlet.rb
+++ b/spec/support/dummy_server/servlet.rb
@@ -149,7 +149,7 @@ def do_#{method.upcase}(req, res)
       res.body   = req.body
     end
 
-    get "/hello world" do |_req, res|
+    get "/héllö-wörld".b do |_req, res|
       res.status = 200
       res.body   = "hello world"
     end

testCase.title: Requesting a URL whose path contains an embedded newline character
testCase.preconditions: The HTTP client is configured to use a custom URL-normalization step that passes the request path through unchanged (it does not strip whitespace).
steps: Issue a GET request for a path that contains a literal newline character in the middle of it, e.g. a path like "/hello" followed by a newline followed by "world".
Observe what the client does before anything is transmitted over the network.
testCase.expectedResult: The client refuses to send the request and raises an error describing the request URI as invalid, rather than transmitting a request line containing an embedded newline character to the server.

metadata.feature: HTTP request line construction with custom URI normalizers

provenance.note: The PR adds specs asserting an error is raised when a custom URI normalizer returns a path or host containing whitespace/newlines. At the base commit no such check exists, so the request proceeds and the malformed request line would be sent instead of raising.

pr.title: fix: pluralize Albanian million scale
pr.description: Albanian number-to-words output now uses the plural scale word for 'million' whenever the million count is greater than one, while preserving the singular form for exactly one million. Previously, compound values such as 12,345,678 rendered the plural count with the singular scale word. The locale data follows the official CLDR Albanian spellout rules, and dedicated Albanian-locale coverage protects both singular and plural output.

pr.title: Fix #2348 - ignore non-String environment properties (ClassCastException)
pr.description: The property-loading routine cast every entry of a Java Properties object to string key/value pairs. Properties can legally hold non-String keys or values (for example after replacing the system properties with arbitrary objects at runtime), and the hard cast then threw a ClassCastException during application startup. The change filters to string-keyed entries and ignores (with a debug log) any entry whose key is not a string, instead of crashing, and adds a regression test.
pr.diff:
diff --git a/projects/core/koin-core/src/jvmMain/kotlin/org/koin/core/registry/PropertyRegistryExt.kt b/projects/core/koin-core/src/jvmMain/kotlin/org/koin/core/registry/PropertyRegistryExt.kt
index 16c3c997a..2dcb055ed 100644
--- a/projects/core/koin-core/src/jvmMain/kotlin/org/koin/core/registry/PropertyRegistryExt.kt
+++ b/projects/core/koin-core/src/jvmMain/kotlin/org/koin/core/registry/PropertyRegistryExt.kt
@@ -10,13 +10,20 @@ import java.util.*
 /**
  *Save properties values into PropertyRegister
  */
-@Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
 fun PropertyRegistry.saveProperties(properties: Properties) {
     _koin.logger.debug("load ${properties.size} properties")
 
-    val propertiesMapValues = properties.toMap() as Map<String, String>
-    propertiesMapValues.forEach { (k: String, v: String) ->
-        saveProperty(k, v)
+    // java.util.Properties can legally hold non-String keys/values (e.g. after
+    // System.setProperties(...) with arbitrary objects). The registry is keyed by
+    // String but stores Any values, so keep any String-keyed entry (value as-is)
+    // and only drop non-String keys — instead of hard-casting values to String and
+    // crashing (#2348).
+    properties.forEach { (k, v) ->
+        if (k is String && v != null) {
+            saveProperty(k, v)
+        } else {
+            _koin.logger.debug("ignore property with non-string key '$k'")
+        }
     }
 }
 
diff --git a/projects/core/koin-core/src/jvmTest/kotlin/org/koin/core/EnvironmentPropertiesTest.kt b/projects/core/koin-core/src/jvmTest/kotlin/org/koin/core/EnvironmentPropertiesTest.kt
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..243410e42
--- /dev/null
+++ b/projects/core/koin-core/src/jvmTest/kotlin/org/koin/core/EnvironmentPropertiesTest.kt
@@ -0,0 +1,41 @@
+package org.koin.core
+
+import org.koin.core.annotation.KoinInternalApi
+import org.koin.core.registry.saveProperties
+import org.koin.dsl.koinApplication
+import java.util.Properties
+import kotlin.test.Test
+import kotlin.test.assertEquals
+import kotlin.test.assertSame
+
+/**
+ * Regression test for #2348. java.util.Properties can legally hold non-String keys/values
+ * (e.g. after System.setProperties(...) with arbitrary objects). Koin hard-cast every entry to
+ * String, crashing with ClassCastException on startup. The registry is String-keyed but holds
+ * Any values, so: non-String *keys* are dropped (unaddressable), non-String *values* are kept.
+ */
+@OptIn(KoinInternalApi::class)
+class EnvironmentPropertiesTest {
+
+    @Test
+    fun saveProperties_tolerates_non_string_entries_issue_2348() {
+        val koin = koinApplication { }.koin
+
+        val objectValue = Any()
+        val props = Properties().apply {
+            setProperty("valid.key", "valid.value")
+            // legacy Properties permits arbitrary objects:
+            put("object.value", objectValue) // String key, Any value -> kept (values are Any)
+            put(Any(), Any())                 // non-string key -> dropped
+            put(42, "string.value")           // non-string key -> dropped
+        }
+
+        // must NOT throw ClassCastException
+        koin.propertyRegistry.saveProperties(props)
+
+        // valid string property is saved
+        assertEquals("valid.value", koin.getProperty<String>("valid.key"))
+        // a non-String value under a String key is preserved as-is (registry stores Any)
+        assertSame(objectValue, koin.getProperty<Any>("object.value"))
+    }
+}

pr.title: [OrderedCollections] Share OrderedSet's replace primitive with OrderedDictionary.replaceElement
pr.description: An ordered dictionary's replace-element-at-index operation and an ordered set's replace-member-at-index operation each performed the same 'append the new member, swap it into position, then remove the old one from the end' step inline. This factors that step into a single shared internal primitive used by both. The PR description states this is a behavior-preserving cleanup with no public API change; the existing test suite passes unmodified.

testCase.title: Replacing an element's key at a specific position in an ordered dictionary
testCase.preconditions: An ordered dictionary contains three key-value pairs in insertion order: ("a", 1), ("b", 2), ("c", 3).
steps: Call the operation that replaces the element at position 1 with a new key "z", keeping the same value 2.
Inspect the resulting dictionary's contents and their order.
Attempt the same kind of replace operation again on the updated dictionary, but this time supply a new key that already exists elsewhere in the dictionary (e.g. "a").
testCase.expectedResult: After the first replace, the dictionary contains ("a", 1), ("z", 2), ("c", 3) in that order — the element at position 1 now has the new key with its value unchanged, and overall ordering is preserved. The second attempt, which supplies a key duplicating an existing one, fails with a duplicate-key error rather than silently corrupting the dictionary.

provenance.note: The change only consolidates the internal append/swap/remove mechanics that both OrderedSet and OrderedDictionary already used inline into one shared primitive; the PR states no public API or behavior changes, so the described replace-at-index and duplicate-key-trap behavior holds identically before the refactor.

pr.title: refactor: use the built-in max/min to simplify the code
pr.description: In Go 1.21, the standard library includes built-in max/min functions, which can greatly simplify code that previously implemented the same comparison manually. The change replaces a manual 'if value is negative, clamp to zero' check in the byte-size string parsing helper with an equivalent call to the built-in max function.

testCase.title: Reading a size-in-bytes configuration value when the stored size string is invalid
testCase.preconditions: A configuration key has been set to a string that does not represent a valid positive size, such as "-5MB".
steps: Set a configuration key's value to the string "-5MB".
Retrieve that key's value using the configuration library's size-in-bytes accessor.
testCase.expectedResult: The accessor returns 0 (zero bytes) rather than a negative number, treating the invalid/negative size as zero.

provenance.note: The change replaces a manual 'if size < 0 { size = 0 }' check with an equivalent call to Go's built-in max(size, 0); both forms clamp a negative parsed size to zero, so the size-in-bytes accessor returns 0 for an invalid negative size string both before and after the refactor.
